# The unsafe uses of the repository (owner q112, 2026-11-11: reviewed unsafe
# bodies in runtime/v1 only; value-facts note, Inventory; audit 3 G8,
# 2026-11-12: one inventory for every package). One line per function of a
# non-test Go file of any package that names package unsafe:
#
#   <file> <function> | invariant: <what makes it safe> | review: <who>, <date>
#
# TestUnsafeBodiesListed fails on a use of unsafe outside this list, on a
# line that names no such use, and on a line with no invariant or review.
# The lowering selects an unsafe body from a fact, never from a std name.
#
# Only the runtime/v1 lines are std bodies an emitted program may call
# (q112). runtime/rt is the run-time support every emitted program links;
# its one use reads an interface value's words and never writes through
# them. The other lines are tooling (the gate, the test observer, the
# producer, a prototype) that no emitted program links.
#
# Trust flags. A site where the emitted program skips a check Go would make
# is a row of this one inventory whatever its mechanism, a runtime/v1 body
# or a compiler flag (audit 3 G8). The IR speed tier's bounded-index flag
# (owner q129, 2026-11-11), which removes a Go bounds check, and its escape
# hints are set only from proved facts (q143, 2026-11-12). They are not
# built yet: the unit that builds the flag adds its sites here with their
# fact, their evidence label and their counted gain, and extends
# TestUnsafeBodiesListed to read them.

# runtime/v1: reviewed std bodies (q112).
runtime/v1/exec/exec_spawn_darwin.go execSysctl | invariant: mib, old and n point to live Go values the caller keeps for the call (a [4]int32, a [648]byte kinfo_proc buffer, its length), converted in the call expression (unsafe.Pointer rule 4); the kernel writes at most *n bytes into old | review: NG IA2b-darwin, 2026-11-13; verifier to confirm
runtime/v1/term_unix.go ioctl | invariant: arg points to a live Go value of the exact kernel type the request names, converted in the call expression (unsafe.Pointer rule 4) | review: STD-sh r2 (listed; body unchanged since the 2026-11-02 FFI rule), 2026-11-12
runtime/v1/exchange_linux.go exchangePaths | invariant: law runtime/v1 TestExchangePathsAreTheNames (a seeded property: the host reads exactly each NUL-ended name, a name with an inner NUL is refused with nothing moved; mutant exchange-path-unterminated) states it: pa and pb are NUL-terminated copies of a and b from syscall.BytePtrFromString, live locals converted to uintptr in the Syscall6 call expression (unsafe.Pointer rule 4); renameat2(2) only reads the two paths and writes no memory; law code.Files.ExchangeSwaps under OnTestHost (std code apply.ergo), runtime/v1 TestFSExchangeSwaps and TestFSExchangeIsOneStep | review: SM fallout fix of SEM4b 86e4f2e6e, 2026-11-19; law-proven by TestExchangePathsAreTheNames
runtime/v1/exchange_darwin.go exchangePaths | invariant: law runtime/v1 TestExchangePathsAreTheNames (a seeded property: the host reads exactly each NUL-ended name, a name with an inner NUL is refused with nothing moved; mutant exchange-path-unterminated) states it: pa and pb are NUL-terminated copies of a and b from syscall.BytePtrFromString, live locals converted to uintptr in the Syscall6 call expression (unsafe.Pointer rule 4); renameatx_np (SYS_RENAMEATX_NP 488) with RENAME_SWAP only reads the two paths and writes no memory; same laws and tests as the linux body, run on the Mac lane (SEM4c darwin-result.md) | review: SM fallout fix of SEM4b 86e4f2e6e, 2026-11-19; law-proven by TestExchangePathsAreTheNames
runtime/v1/actor_trace.go - | invariant: graphKey holds two type words (typeID) only as map-key identities; nothing dereferences or converts them back to a value | review: batch-19 integrator (listed; binsize BS2 body, reviewed in batch 18), 2026-11-14; verifier to confirm
runtime/v1/actor_trace.go typeID | invariant: an interface value of a non-nil type is two words, the first its type word, which the Go runtime keeps once per type; the word is read, never written, and used only as an identity | review: batch-19 integrator (listed; binsize BS2 body, reviewed in batch 18), 2026-11-14; verifier to confirm
runtime/rt/text.go nilPointer | invariant: reads the data word of its own parameter's interface value through a pointer to that live parameter; the word is compared with nil, never dereferenced | review: batch-19 integrator (listed; binsize BS2 body, reviewed in batch 18), 2026-11-15; verifier to confirm
scripts/stdcount/perf_linux.go countInstructions | invariant: a is a live perf_event_attr local whose size is its own unsafe.Sizeof, converted in the call expression (rule 4); the read's buffer is v's 24 bytes, three live uint64s | review: batch-19 integrator (listed; batch-18 body), 2026-11-15; verifier to confirm
lint/memory_linux.go limitMemory | invariant: limit is a live syscall.Rlimit local, converted to uintptr in the call expression (unsafe.Pointer rule 4); prlimit64 only writes no old limit (nil) and reads the new one | review: batch-19 integrator (listed; LINT3 body), 2026-11-15; verifier to confirm
runtime/v1/exec/exec_sandbox_linux.go sbMountSetattr | invariant: p and &attr point to live Go values of the exact kernel types mount_setattr(2) reads (a NUL-terminated path, struct mount_attr of its size), converted in the call expression (unsafe.Pointer rule 4), p kept alive past the call; it runs only in the sandbox helper before its exec | review: TH1b implementor, 2026-11-15 (closure's mountSetattr, the sweep's)
runtime/v1/exec/exec_sandbox_linux.go sbDropPrivileges | invariant: header and sets are live Go values of capset(2)'s exact types (version 3, two data words), converted in the call expression (unsafe.Pointer rule 4); it runs only in the sandbox helper, on its locked thread, before its exec | review: TH1b implementor, 2026-11-15 (closure's dropPrivileges, the sweep's)
runtime/v1/owned.go StringsBuilderTextOwned | invariant: the lowering calls it only on a consumed buffer (types.md, Bindings 2), so no code writes buf[0:len(buf)] after the call; Ergo writes a slice's bytes only through a binding that holds it | review: STD-sh r2 implementor, 2026-11-12; verifier to confirm
runtime/v1/host.go HostRoot.ReadFile | invariant: the string is the bytes of the slice os.Root.ReadFile made for this call, which nothing else holds and nothing writes after it returns; its length is the slice's length (unsafe.String over SliceData), and an empty or nil slice gives "" | review: NG HTTP-FAST-c9, 2026-11-18; verifier to confirm
runtime/v1/host.go FSMapFile | invariant: the string names a PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED mapping that is never unmapped, so its bytes never change and stay mapped while the program runs (a file truncated by another process faults with SIGBUS, documented in stdlib.md fs note 4); TestFSMapFileKeepsItsInvariant | review: 1BRC implementor (listed at the merge of FU-audit's inventory into BCE1), 2026-11-12; verifier to confirm
runtime/v1/view.go BytesView | invariant: the lowering calls it only as a whole argument of a Go call at a parameter whose reads fact is validated (a row of internal/gofacts with View set, its guard line current in the shipped ledger) and with no callback or written operand at the call (lower/view.go); the slice's capacity is its length, so an append copies; Go never writes, keeps or returns it, so the string's bytes stay as Ergo holds them; every test build takes GuardBytes instead | review: LF2b implementor (owner q193), 2026-11-16; verifier to confirm
runtime/v1/guard_unix.go BytesGuard.mapPages | invariant: takes the address of mem[0] of a live mapping it just made, to register its range with rt for fault naming; the address is compared, never dereferenced | review: LF2b implementor, 2026-11-16; verifier to confirm
runtime/v1/unchecked.go ByteAt | invariant: the lowering calls it only where a bounds fact proves 0 <= i < len(s) and s is not written between the proof and the load (lower/bounds.go; fact label checked, run build only; factLowering=checked keeps Go's index); TestBoundsFactsSound, TestBoundsFactsAgree | review: BCE1 implementor, 2026-11-12; verifier to confirm
runtime/v1/unchecked.go StringAt | invariant: the lowering calls it only where a bounds fact proves 0 <= i <= j <= len(s); an empty result is "", so no string points one past s's bytes (lower/bounds.go); TestBoundsFactsSound, TestBoundsFactsAgree | review: BCE1 implementor, 2026-11-12; verifier to confirm
runtime/v1/unchecked.go StringN | invariant: the lowering calls it only where a bounds fact proves 0 <= i and i+n <= len(s), for a constant n > 0, from s[a:a+n] of one sum of locals (lower/bounds.go, sliceLen); TestBoundsFactsSound, TestBoundsFactsAgree | review: BCE1 implementor, 2026-11-12; verifier to confirm
runtime/v1/unchecked.go stringOf | invariant: p points inside a live string's bytes and the n > 0 bytes from p stay inside them (its callers StringAt and StringN); the header struct has a string's layout, a pointer then an int, so the conversion of *struct to *string is rule 1 of unsafe.Pointer | review: BCE1 implementor, 2026-11-12; verifier to confirm
runtime/v1/unchecked.go AddrAt | invariant: the lowering calls it only for a read where a bounds fact proves 0 <= i < len(xs), so the address lies inside xs's array (lower/bounds.go); TestBoundsFactsSound, TestBoundsFactsAgree | review: BCE1 implementor, 2026-11-12; verifier to confirm

# runtime/rt: run-time support.
runtime/rt/trace.go - | invariant: ident mirrors the two words of a Go interface value (type word, data word), the layout the gc compiler has used since Go 1.4; ident is compared, never dereferenced, so a layout change gives wrong origins (TestTraceEqualFailuresNameTheirOwnOccurrence fails), not memory errors | review: FU-audit implementor (no unsafe-free form keeps a boxed value's identity: reflect exposes no address of a non-addressable value), 2026-11-12; verifier to confirm
runtime/rt/park_word.go gopark | invariant: the linkname declaration of runtime.gopark, whose signature Go keeps for linking packages (go.dev/issue/67401); a *g is passed as its address and the two reasons as their uint8 type; TestParkWordLinksTheRuntime checks the declaration and both reason numbers against the release's source | review: PARK1 implementor, 2026-11-17; verifier to confirm
runtime/rt/park_word.go wordParker.park | invariant: the lock argument is the address of the parker's own word, which lives in a heap Task kept by the parked waiter's frame for the whole park; gopark passes it back only to parkCommit | review: PARK1 implementor, 2026-11-17; verifier to confirm
runtime/rt/park_word.go parkCommit | invariant: w is the word park passed; it runs on the system stack, so it is nosplit, allocates nothing and stores an integer (the g's address, kept live by allgs), never a Go pointer, so it needs no write barrier | review: PARK1 implementor, 2026-11-17; verifier to confirm
runtime/rt/trace.go identOf | invariant: reads the two words of its own parameter's interface value through a pointer to that parameter, which is live for the read; the words are copied as pointers, so the stored value stays reachable while an ident of it is held next to the failure that holds it | review: FU-audit implementor, 2026-11-12; verifier to confirm
